accounting_notes: This is the receivables summary screen. "Outstanding dues $1.84M" is the estate-wide Accounts Receivable control total. It TIES EXACTLY to the "Arrears by phase" panel: Phase 1 $412k + Phase 2 $589k + Phase 3 $293k + Phase 4 $474k + Phase 5 $72k = $1,840k = $1.84M. Any rebuild must make the AR control account equal the sum of the per-phase arrears sub-totals, which in turn must equal the sum of the per-household Balance figures on screen 04. The "↑ 4%" warn chip is a period-over-period movement on that same control total (arrears rising is styled as a warning, not as growth). The activity row "Payment received — Lot 47 · $6,200" is a cash receipt and would post Dr Bank/Cash $6,200 / Cr Accounts Receivable – Lot 47 $6,200, reducing both the unit sub-ledger balance and the AR control. RECONCILIATION WARNING: Lot 47 (Andrea Fletcher, Phase 2 · Lot 47 on screen 04) still shows a Balance of $12,400 after this $6,200 receipt, and $12,400 = exactly 2 × $6,200 — so the board implies a standard periodic maintenance charge of $6,200 per unit and leaves ambiguous whether the Balance column is as-of-now (post-receipt) or as-of-last-statement (pre-receipt). No account codes, no debit/credit columns, no trial balance, no ageing buckets and no bank reconciliation appear on this screen; arrears are shown as a single net figure per phase with no ageing split.

Headings and figures verbatim: "Total outstanding" $1.84M · "Current" $612k · "30 days" $498k · "60 days" $421k · "90+ days" $309k. TIE: the four ageing buckets sum exactly to the total — 612 + 498 + 421 + 309 = 1,840 (thousand) = $1.84M, so Total outstanding is a DERIVED control figure and must equal the sum of the buckets. The buckets are the four canonical AR ageing bands (0–29 / 30–59 / 60–89 / 90+ days past due). PER-UNIT SUBSIDIARY LEDGER: each table row is one unit's AR sub-ledger balance and its single worst ageing bucket — $12,400 (30 days), $31,600 (90+ days), $6,200 (Current), $18,600 (60 days), $44,900 (90+ days). The .content block holds a SINGLE inline-styled card and nothing else: div style="background:var(--white);border:1px solid var(--navy-100);border-radius:16px;overflow:hidden;". No subnav, no KPI row, no table, no empty state, no footer buttons on this screen.

Inside the card are five .filing-row flex rows (align-items:center, gap 14px, padding 14px 16px, 1px --navy-100 bottom border, removed on last-child). Each row has exactly four children in this order: .filing-icon (38x38, radius 11px, --navy-100 fill, holding a 17x17 --navy-600 SVG; the .warn modifier swaps the fill to --amber-100 and the stroke to --amber-700), then .filing-txt (flex:1) containing .ft1 (13px 700 navy-900) over .ft2 (10.5px slate-500), then .filing-due (11px 600 slate-500, fixed width:120px), then a .status-badge pill.

Row 1: .filing-icon.warn with an exclamation-in-circle SVG; ft1 "S01 — Statutory Deduction Remittance"; ft2 "August 2026 · NIS, NHT, Education Tax, PAYE" (middot separator); due "Due Sep 14"; badge .status-badge.pending "Due soon".
Row 2: plain .filing-icon with a document/page-fold SVG; ft1 "S01 — Statutory Deduction Remittance"; ft2 "July 2026"; due "Filed Aug 12"; badge .status-badge.approved "Filed".
Row 3: plain .filing-icon document SVG; ft1 "S02 — Monthly Reconciliation"; ft2 "July 2026"; due "Filed Aug 12"; badge .status-badge.approved "Filed".
Row 4: plain .filing-icon document SVG; ft1 "GCT Return"; ft2 "August 2026"; due "Filed Sep 1"; badge .status-badge.approved "Filed".
Row 5: plain .filing-icon with a calendar SVG (rect plus "M3 10h18M8 3v4M16 3v4"); ft1 "P24 — Annual Employer Return"; ft2 "Tax year 2025"; due "Due Mar 31, 2027"; badge .status-badge.draft "Not started".

accounting_notes:
No figures are printed on this screen, but every row is a clearing event against a control account and the linkages must be modelled.

• "S01 — Statutory Deduction Remittance" for "August 2026 · NIS, NHT, Education Tax, PAYE", due Sep 14, status "Due soon". This is the remittance that clears the four statutory payable control accounts credited by the August 2026 pay run on screen 15: NIS 13,200 + NHT 8,800 + Education Tax 9,603 + PAYE 85,392 = 116,995, which is exactly the "Total deductions" figure $116,995 on that run. Paying it is DR the four payable controls / CR Bank 116,995, returning those controls to nil for August.
• "S01 — Statutory Deduction Remittance", July 2026, Filed Aug 12, status Filed — the same clearing already completed for the July run (whose gross/net of $440,000 / $323,005 on screen 13 implies the same $116,995 of deductions).
• "S02 — Monthly Reconciliation", July 2026, Filed Aug 12 — the reconciliation form that agrees the July S01 remittance to the July payroll register; it is the reconciliation control tying payroll deductions per employee to the amount actually remitted. It is filed on the same date as the July S01, so the two are submitted as a pair.
• "GCT Return", August 2026, Filed Sep 1 — a separate output/input tax return, not payroll; it clears the GCT payable/receivable control rather than the statutory deduction controls.
• "P24 — Annual Employer Return", Tax year 2025, Due Mar 31, 2027, "Not started" — the annual employer return that must reconcile the full year of monthly S01/S02 filings to the annual payroll totals per employee.

Due-date rules implied: S01 for a month is due the 14th of the following month (August → Sep 14); the annual P24 is due Mar 31. No ageing buckets, no trial balance and no running balance appear on this screen.

accounting_notes: No account codes, debit/credit columns, trial balance, ageing bucket or running balance are drawn on this screen — the only ledger-bearing column is "Deposit". Transcribe exactly: "$5,000 held" (Gazebo, Andrea Fletcher — Lot 47, Confirmed), "$6,000 — awaiting payment" (Club House, Sonia Campbell — Lot 88, Pending), "$10,000 held" (Community Centre, Keith Walters — Lot 63, Confirmed), "$5,000 refunded Aug 18" (Gazebo, Rachel Bennett — Lot 3, Completed). Currency is written with a bare "$" and comma thousands separator, with NO decimal places and NO J$ prefix, unlike the ledger boards. Three distinct deposit states must each map to a posting: (a) "held" — cash received from the resident and carried as a refundable liability, so Dr Cash/Bank, Cr Amenity Deposits Held (a liability control account); the held balance implied by this screen is 5,000 + 10,000 = 15,000, which is a DERIVED sum of the two Confirmed rows and is not itself printed anywhere on the board. (b) "awaiting payment" — the $6,000 is a quoted/expected deposit only, with no cash movement yet; it must NOT be posted to the deposits-held liability or it will overstate the control account by 6,000. It is at most a receivable raised against the resident's unit ledger, and the booking sits at status Pending until it clears. (c) "refunded Aug 18" — the reversal of a previously held deposit: Dr Amenity Deposits Held 5,000, Cr Cash/Bank 5,000, dated Aug 18, three days after the Aug 15 event date; the row's status becomes Completed and the deposit no longer forms part of the held balance. Each deposit figure ties one-for-one to amenity.deposit_amount on screen 20 (Gazebo $5,000, Club House $6,000, Community Centre $10,000), so the deposit control account per amenity reconciles as: sum of deposits held = count of confirmed bookings × that amenity's configured deposit. Note the booking fee (a real revenue item, $3,000 / $4,500 / $8,000 on screen 20) is NOT shown in this Deposit column at all — fee revenue and refundable deposit are separate postings and must not be conflated in one figure.

accounting_notes: This screen shows no account codes, debits, credits, control accounts, ageing buckets or running balances — it is the rate card that SOURCES the postings made elsewhere, so the figures must be transcribed exactly because everything on screen 19 and every amenity charge on the unit ledger derives from them. Booking fee (revenue, earned and non-refundable): Gazebo $3,000, Club House $4,500, Community Centre $8,000, Pool Deck "Free for residents" (nil). Deposit (refundable liability, not revenue): Gazebo $5,000, Club House $6,000, Community Centre $10,000, Pool Deck "None" (nil). These are two structurally different amounts on the same card and must post to different accounts: a booking fee is Dr Resident/Unit receivable, Cr Amenity Income when the booking is confirmed; a deposit is Dr Cash/Bank, Cr Amenity Deposits Held (liability) on receipt and reversed on refund — never recognised as income. The deposit column reconciles directly to screen 19: Gazebo $5,000 held matches Gazebo deposit $5,000, Community Centre $10,000 held matches Community Centre deposit $10,000, Club House $6,000 awaiting payment matches Club House deposit $6,000, and the refunded Gazebo booking of $5,000 matches the same Gazebo figure — i.e. bookings copy amenity.deposit_amount verbatim, so a change to this rate card must not retro-alter deposits already held or the deposit control account will no longer agree to the sum of open bookings. A Pool Deck booking generates no fee posting and no deposit posting at all, so nil-value amenities must be allowed to produce a booking with zero journal lines rather than a zero-amount entry. accounting_notes: This is a charge-posting screen with an explicit GL coding and a running-balance preview. GL account field reads exactly "4000 — Maintenance Fee Income" — a revenue account, so posting this charge credits 4000 Maintenance Fee Income for $15,000.00 and debits the Accounts Receivable / member dues control account for the unit (Phase 2 · Lot 47 — Andrea Fletcher). The charge type is "Special assessment" and the amount is "$15,000.00" (two-decimal form in the form field). The "Ledger preview" panel is the unit's receivable sub-ledger running balance, shown in whole-dollar form without decimals: "Current balance" $12,400; "+ New charge" $15,000; a border-top rule then "New balance" $27,400. New balance is DERIVED: 12,400 + 15,000 = 27,400, i.e. opening unit AR balance plus the new debit. The preview note states the charge "is added to her existing 30-day ageing bucket" — so the ageing schedule buckets by days outstanding and this charge lands in the 30-day bucket rather than starting a new current bucket, even though its due date is "Oct 15, 2026". Ties: unit ledger balance ($27,400) must equal the sum of the unit's posted charges less payments; the 4000 revenue credit must tie to the AR control account total across all units; the $15,000.00 form amount and the $15,000 preview line are the same figure formatted differently and must not diverge.
